question.text: Chapter 9 (Waterfall application): 'Himalaya Growth Fund' (Cat II PE) has INR 500 cr committed; total contributed INR 400 cr at exit; gross returns INR 800 cr. Fund has an 8% hurdle, 100% catch-up, then 80/20 carry (European whole-fund waterfall). LPs receive 100% until (a) return of contributed 400 cr and (b) 8% preferred return. Approximate carry to GP (ignoring management fee)?

answer.text: Approximately INR 80 crore — with a full 100% catch-up, the GP ultimately ends up with 20% of total profit once preferred return + catch-up + 80/20 split are stacked.
Approximately INR 60 crore — after return of capital and 8% preferred only, with no catch-up.

explanation.text: The Logic: Assume a 3-year fund life. Contributed capital = 400 cr; total profit = 800 - 400 = 400 cr. Preferred return at 8% on 400 cr ≈ 400 × (1.08^3 - 1) ≈ 103.88 cr. Stage 1: LPs receive 400 + 103.88 = 503.88 cr. Stage 2 (100% catch-up): GP gets 103.88 × 20/80 ≈ 25.97 cr. Stage 3: remaining 800 - 503.88 - 25.97 = 270.15 cr split 80/20 → GP gets 270.15 × 0.20 ≈ 54.03 cr. Total GP carry ≈ 25.97 + 54.03 ≈ 80 cr. With a full 100% catch-up the GP ends up with ≈ 20% of total profit (400 × 20% = 80 cr), which is the canonical waterfall result. The Trap: Option A understates sharply. Option C drops the catch-up step and so under-states the GP's share. Option D treats carry as 20% of gross proceeds without netting return-of-capital or hurdle — the classic distractor. Note: The workbook's waterfall mechanics (European, preferred return, catch-up, residual split) are described on pages 92, 125 and 173; the INR 80 crore figure is purely the application of those mechanics to the stated stem with full catch-up.
